subject: Post-demo: EmberCare integration scope, SDK/auth & model-routing recommendations
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira@embercare.health>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-22T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: EmberCare integration scope, SDK/auth & model-routing recommendations

Hi Samira — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

1) Integration checklist (low friction MVP):
   - SDK: use our JS SDK for server-side inference; we recommend server-to-Redwood via mTLS + API key for now.
   - Auth: EmberCare will use their existing IdP for user auth; for API layer we propose short-lived API keys rotated by your infra (we can accept a gateway token or Vault integration).
   - Routing: start with single-region us-west for pilot; add eu fallback later.

2) Model routing & fallback suggestion:
   - Production routing policy: prefer high-throughput variant (redwood-medium-quant) for non-interactive batch embeddings and rerankers; route chat/interactive flows to redwood-low-latency variant.
   - Fallback chain: primary -> medium-quant; if CPU/GPU backpressure -> small-quant fallback; if region outage -> cross-region fallback to us-east.

3) Structured output / tool-calling:
   - We'll enable the structured output schema for intake forms (JSON output) and a deterministic post-filter for PHI redaction.
   - For tool-calling (appointment lookups), we recommend our function-calling hooks with signed webhook responses.

Attachments: I attached a one-page auth playbook and an integration matrix to map responsibilities (see embercare_integration_matrix.xlsx, embercare_auth_playbook.pdf).

Next steps: 
- Samira: confirm owner for infra/credentials and whether EmberCare prefers Vault or static key rotation.
- Ben & Tessa: I will schedule an architecture run-through next Wed with your infra lead.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

---
Aisha Rahman
Redwood Inference
From: Samira Khan <samira@embercare.health>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Luca Moretti <luca@embercare.health>
Date: 2026-08-23T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: EmberCare integration scope, SDK/auth & model-routing recommendations

Thanks Aisha — really helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Auth: we prefer Vault for secrets management and would like short-lived tokens issued by our platform (EmberVault). Can your team accept tokens that rotate every 30 minutes?
- Latency policy: for inbound triage chat we need p95 < 350ms; is that achievable with your low-latency variant in us-west?
- PHI redaction: can you share the deterministic redaction rules you mentioned? We need them for our compliance team.

I'll loop in Luca (infra) to coordinate credentials. He can join the run-through next Wed.

Samira
Head of Product, EmberCare Health

Date: 2026-08-24T11:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: EmberCare integration scope, SDK/auth & model-routing recommendations

Adding some technical notes ahead of the run-through: 

- Token rotation: Redwood supports short-lived tokens from customer KMS/Vault; 30-minute TTL is fine. We recommend a gateway token with a service-to-service exchange to avoid per-request overhead.

- p95 latency target: for chat with sequence lengths ~150 tokens and batch size 1, redwood-low-latency in us-west typically achieves p95 ~280-320ms depending on concurrent QPS. We'll instrument and set an SLO for the pilot.

- Structured output & PHI: attaching a short redaction guide (see embercare_auth_playbook.pdf). For deterministic redaction we use token-level blocklists + regex rules and an optional post-generation classifier for edge cases.

- Routing policy config (example snippet):
   - route("triage-chat") -> policy(prefer=low-latency, max_latency=350ms, fallbacks=[medium-quant, small-quant], region=us-west)
   - embeddings/rerank -> policy(prefer=medium-quant, batch_window_ms=50, region=us-west)

I'll prep a proposed routing YAML and attach before the session.

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: embercare_routing_example.yaml (text)
From: Luca Moretti <luca@embercare.health>

Date: 2026-08-25T08:41:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: EmberCare integration scope, SDK/auth & model-routing recommendations

Thanks Ben — that all sounds reasonable. A couple of practical items from infra: 

- We'll provision an EmberVault role with a service account for Redwood and a short-lived token exchange endpoint. Expect initial creds by EOD Monday.
- For the pilot, we want telemetry exported to our Splunk instance. Can Redwood send per-request traces and token-cost metrics to a customer webhook?

Also — curious about the reranker: if we run reranking as a two-step embeddings + reranker flow, what's the recommended throughput/instance sizing? We currently expect peak 1200 reqs/min for search.

Luca
Infra Lead, EmberCare

Great progress — confirming next steps and owners before the architecture session: 

- EmberCare (Samira / Luca): provide Vault role and token-exchange endpoint; share estimated QPS pattern (peak, baseline) for reranker by Monday.
- Redwood (Ben): send routing YAML and a sizing recommendation for the two-step embeddings+rerank (estimate for 1200 reqs/min).
- Redwood (Aisha / Tessa): schedule the technical run-through (requested Wed 2026-08-28 10:00 PT) and invite EmberCare infra + security.

Quick answers to Luca's Qs: 
- Telemetry: yes — Redwood can push traces and per-request metrics to a customer webhook. We'll include an example payload.
- Reranker throughput: for 1200req/min we recommend a small pool of dedicated GPU pods for embeddings (batched) and a separate low-latency CPU/GPU combo for rerankers; Ben will send concrete instance counts.

I'll set a calendar invite for Wed and include the pre-read (routing YAML, auth playbook, cost estimates).

Thanks — looking forward to the run-through.

Tessa Morgan
Sales Engineer Lead, Redwood Inference
